<reason>Side B won decisively by establishing what "as strict as traditional media" actually adds beyond existing consumer-protection rules against buried #ad tags, and proving why broadcast-style rules backfire in unscripted creator media. Side A walked into a fatal contradiction on Side B's two-year-old gifted microphone example—first biting the bullet in [A2.3] that simply using the microphone for two years requires disclosure, then implying the opposite in [A3.1], and finally trying to rewrite [A2.3] in [A4.1]. Side B exposed this inconsistency cleanly, dismantled Side A's conflation of contract lawyers with live broadcast standards-and-practices screening, and showed that importing closed-set broadcast liability into unscripted livestreams would trigger defensive blanket disclaimers that obscure real paid promotions.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>In [B3.1] and [B4.1]-[B4.2], Side B trapped Side A in a direct contradiction over whether using a gifted microphone two years later requires disclosure, quoting [A2.3] verbatim to defeat Side A's attempt in [A4.1] to claim it had only meant active product reviews.</best_rebuttal>
